Extract Submodels and Coefficients from MID Models

Source: R/methods_mid.R
subset.mid.Rd

subset() and coef() methods for extracting a subset of component functions from a fitted MID model ("mid" / "midrib") or a collection of models ("mids"). subset() returns a lightweight submodel object, while coef() returns a named list of the fitted intercept and component effect tables.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mid'
subset(x, terms = NULL, intercept = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mids'
subset(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mid'
coef(object, terms = NULL, intercept = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'midrib'
coef(object, ...)

Arguments

x, object

a fitted model object ("mid", "midrib", or "mids" for subset()).

terms

an optional character vector, formula, or terms object specifying the subset of terms (and intercept) to retain or extract. Defaults to all terms in the model.

intercept

logical. If TRUE, the intercept is preserved or included; if FALSE, it is zeroed out or omitted. If NULL (default), inferred from terms.

...

further arguments passed to methods.

Value

subset() returns a "mid" (or "mids") object containing only the selected component functions. coef() returns a named list containing the intercept (if included) and data frames of component effects (excluding .density) for each matched term.

See also

interpret, predict.mid

Examples

data(airquality, package = "datasets")
mid <- interpret(Ozone ~ Wind * Temp, airquality, k = c(5, 3))
#> 'model' not passed: response variable in 'data' is used

# Extract a submodel containing only Wind and Temp
submid <- subset(mid, ~ Wind + Temp)
predict(submid, head(airquality), type = "terms")
#>           Wind      Temp
#> [1,] -6.259685 -15.91298
#> [2,] -5.589946 -12.92598
#> [3,] -8.243855 -10.81277
#> [4,] -7.588329 -18.32599
#> [5,] -9.256941 -20.73899
#> [6,] -9.614501 -16.39558
#> attr(,"constant")
#> [1] 42.12931

# Extract component effect tables without the intercept
coef(mid, terms = c("Wind", "Wind:Temp"), intercept = FALSE)
#> $Wind
#>   Wind    .effect
#> 1  2.3  73.163877
#> 2  7.4  -6.259685
#> 3  9.7  -3.692354
#> 4 11.5  -7.588329
#> 5 20.7 -13.070913
#> 
#> $`Wind:Temp`
#>   Wind Temp     .effect
#> 1  2.3   57 -34.2733452
#> 2  9.7   57  -0.4128318
#> 3 20.7   57   7.2118188
#> 4  2.3   79  39.6965554
#> 5  9.7   79  -9.4929815
#> 6 20.7   79   0.2151154
#> 7  2.3   97 -56.7056946
#> 8  9.7   97  38.4237835
#> 9 20.7   97 -42.5028164
#>
